topic: Decide which programming language for a new internal tool

scenario.topic: Decide which programming language for a new internal tool
scenario.opening_question: What trade-offs are you most willing to make between development speed, maintainability, and integration?

options.name: Python 3.10 with Django Framework
options.upside: Fast prototyping with many libraries and strong community
options.tradeoff: Moderate runtime performance may affect scalability under heavy load
options.concern: Some team members have limited Django experience

options.name: TypeScript with React and Node.js Backend
options.upside: Strong type safety reduces runtime errors and improves maintainability
options.tradeoff: Longer initial setup and steeper learning curve for backend integration
options.concern: Requires more upfront effort and familiarity with full-stack JavaScript

options.name: Go 1.20 with Gin Web Framework
options.upside: High performance and easy deployment with compiled binaries
options.tradeoff: Smaller ecosystem and fewer ready-made libraries than Python or JavaScript
options.concern: Team has limited Go experience, increasing ramp-up time

options.name: C# with .NET Core and Blazor
options.upside: Robust tooling and good integration with existing Windows infrastructure
options.tradeoff: Potential overhead in deployment and licensing concerns in some environments
options.concern: Less community support outside Microsoft ecosystem compared to open source

shared_context: The team has exactly 4 members involved in the decision
The internal tool must be ready within 3 months
Budget for new technology licenses is limited
